summary: Pietro Merlo was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Turin (1867–1871), studying with Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. He taught at Naples (1877) and the University of Pavia (1877–1888).
Ping-kun Chen specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate at National Taiwan University (2001–2010), where he later served as an assistant professor beginning in 2012.

Piotr Balcerowicz is a Polish Indologist and philosopher. Educated at the University of Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, University of Hamburg (Dr. phil., 1999), and Polish Academy of Sciences, he served as professor at SWPS University (2008–2011) and University of Warsaw (from 2011).

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his PhD under Jerzy Bańczerowski at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, having also studied under teachers including Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Piyanjali de Zoysa works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a B.A. from the University of Delhi (1990–1995) and a Ph.D. from the University of Colombo (2002–2006), where she became Professor in Clinical Psychology in 1997.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught figures including Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian scholar in linguistics, Indology, and archaeology. He earned a doctorate at Leiden University (1921–1926) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He later served as professor at Gadjah Mada University, University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis (Ph.D., ~1974–1980), also training under Philip Kapleau. In 1994, she joined the University of Vermont.

Pongsit Pangsrivongse works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Cambridge (B.A., 2011–2015) and University of Oxford (D.Phil., 2020–2023), he worked as a Thai diplomat (2015–2024) before joining the University of Vienna in 2025.

Pooja Tomar is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Delhi (2013–2019) and earned a PhD from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University in 2022, where she has also served as a research scholar.

Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad was active in Indology and archaeology. He served as State Engineer in the Junagadh State Engineer's Office, Chief Engineer for Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Park studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Bristol, and completed doctoral research under Rupert Gethin. At Chulalongkorn University, he served as a special lecturer (attested 2011) and program chair (2024).

Poul Tuxen was a Danish scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Copenhagen, also studying at Leipzig and Bonn. He served as Professor of Indology at Copenhagen from 1928 to 1951.
Poulami Ray is an archaeology and history scholar. Ray studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He has held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as a professor in 2009.
Prabhasa Dharma was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Dharma studied under traditional teachers Joshu Sasaki, beginning in 1967, and Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi was an Indian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, later serving at Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.
Prabodh Shirvalkar is an archaeologist and Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. in 2009 at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he became an assistant professor that same year.

Prachi Vatsal specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed an M.Phil.–PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2016–2023) and was appointed as a Sanskrit Educator at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi in 2025.
